projectDir.description: Directory holding the project, relative to the directory the CLI runs in.

version-declared.name: Elixir version is declared
version-declared.description: The project declares the Elixir version it compiles against, and that version is no older than the configured floor.
version-declared.remediation:
Declare the Elixir version in the `project` function of `mix.exs`, where the project already describes itself:

```elixir
def project do
  [
    app: :widget,
    version: "1.2.3",
    elixir: "~> 1.16"
  ]
end
```

Without it, Mix compiles with whatever Elixir the runner has installed, so a macro or standard library difference between releases shows up in CI instead of on the laptop that introduced it.

minVersion.description: Oldest Elixir version accepted. A declared version below this is a violation.

lockfile-committed.name: Elixir dependencies are locked
lockfile-committed.description: The project commits `mix.lock`, so fetching the same commit resolves the same packages and verifies them.
lockfile-committed.remediation:
Resolve your dependencies once and commit the lock file Mix writes:

```bash
mix deps.get
git add mix.lock
```

`mix.lock` pins every package to one version along with its checksum. Without it, an application resolves whatever Hex serves that day and checks nothing against what was reviewed.

no-git-dependencies.name: No dependency is fetched from git
no-git-dependencies.description: No dependency the project declares is fetched from a git repository.
no-git-dependencies.remediation:
Take the dependency from Hex instead of from a git repository:

```elixir
{:widget_ui, "~> 1.4"}
```

If the package is yours and unpublished, publish it to a private Hex organisation. A `git:` or `github:` tuple tracks a branch its owner can move or force push. It is also compiled from source at fetch time, not taken from a release Hex has published and checksummed, so two builds of the same commit can compile different code.
